newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan bans import of Afghan bones.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan bans import of Afghan bones.

text.p: Pakistan banned the import of animal bones from war-ravaged Afghanistan on Wednesday amid fears that they might be mixed with human bones.
"The government of Pakistan has decided to impose a ban on the import of animal bones from Afghanistan with immediate effect," a Commerce Ministry statement said.
"The decision has been taken in view of reports appearing in a section of the foreign press suggesting the possibility of export of human bones from Afghanistan to Pakistan," it said.
The allegations would be investigated before the ban was lifted, the statement added.
There has been a brisk trade in animal bones dug up in Afghanistan by impoverished people desperate for a livelihood after 18 years of conflict that has wrecked the economy.
More than 3,000 people scavenge for bones on one rubbish tip outside Kabul alone, selling what they collect to wholesalers for the equivalent of about 50 U.S. cents a kilogram.
The bones are then exported to Pakistan to be turned into soap and oil.
An article published in the London Times last month said that Afghans were exhuming human bones from graveyards and selling them as animal bones.
Workers on the Kabul rubbish dump have denied the report, saying that no Moslem would be involved in such a trade.
